title: Set sign-in frequency for high-risk Copilot users
problem: Executives with broad data access stay signed in for weeks on shared or traveling devices.
steps: Policy 1: Conditional Access policy for the exec group targeting Office 365; Session: Sign-in frequency, e.g. every 12 hours.

Policy 2 (separate): Persistent browser session = Never persistent. This control requires the policy to target All resources, so it can't live in the Office 365 policy — scope it with a device filter or to unmanaged devices.
Turn off 'Remember MFA on trusted devices' before using sign-in frequency to avoid unexpected prompts.
pitfalls: Too frequent prompts cause MFA fatigue — balance with phishing-resistant methods.
done_when: The exec group has a sign-in frequency policy on Office 365.
A separate policy sets Never persistent browser session, scoped with a device filter or to unmanaged devices.
'Remember MFA on trusted devices' is off.

troubleshooting.symptom: Users get more MFA prompts than the configured frequency suggests.
troubleshooting.cause: 'Remember MFA on trusted devices' is still on alongside sign-in frequency.
troubleshooting.fix: Turn it off, as in the steps.

troubleshooting.symptom: The Never persistent browser session control can't be saved in the Office 365 policy.
troubleshooting.cause: That control requires the policy to target All resources.
troubleshooting.fix: Keep it in a separate All resources policy scoped with a device filter or to unmanaged devices.
Lengthen the interval and move users to phishing-resistant methods rather than removing the control.

rollback: Entra ID > Conditional Access > Policies: open Policy 1 (sign-in frequency) and/or Policy 2 (persistent browser session), one at a time and set Enable policy to Report-only (keeps impact data) or Off. Don't delete it, so the configuration is kept.
Confirm in the sign-in logs (Conditional Access tab on the affected events) that the policy no longer applies and sign-ins succeed.
Adjust the interval or scope, then switch back to On.
